title: Iframe Height Test Simulator
description: A mock MicroSim with a canvas, three sliders and two buttons inside an iframe frame whose bottom edge follows an Iframe height slider. Run test sweeps a scan line down the page and marks each control PASS when its bottom is at most the iframe height plus the tolerance. The results panel shows the overall status, the content height and, on failure, the suggested height, as test-iframe-heights.py computes it.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Quality Assurance
Web Development
MicroSim Engineering

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Control visibility and iframe height tests
learningObjectives: The learner will apply the control visibility and iframe height tests to a mock MicroSim by choosing an iframe height, and will calculate the suggested height from the content height.
prerequisites: The CANVAS_HEIGHT comment and iframe heights (Chapter 12)
Bounding boxes and the tester's rules (Chapter 13)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

controls.label: Mock element
controls.action: Show its bounding box and inequality

equations: PASS if bottom <= iframe height + tolerance
assumptions: The rules are those of test-iframe-heights.py: 5 px default tolerance, 10 px safety margin.
limitations: Only bottom edges are checked, as in the real tester; right-edge overflow and overlaps are invisible to it.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate, then verify with an animated test run
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter exploration with a worked check (Apply level)
keyQuestions: What number does each control's bottom edge have to beat?
Where does the suggested height come from?
What can this test not see?
commonMisconceptions: A canvas below the iframe edge fails the test.
The suggested height is the content height plus 2.
A declared CANVAS_HEIGHT changes whether the MicroSim passes.
assessmentOpportunities: The learner computes the pass limit, each verdict and the suggested height for a given set of numbers.
The learner explains why a declared CANVAS_HEIGHT changes the suggestion but not the PASS or FAIL.
